welcome.text: Welcome to the SportVid video analysis platform for scholarly video analysis and sports science.
welcome.demo_text: We are currently preparing a video that demonstrates the features of SportVid and explains how to use it to simplify the onboarding process. It is expected to be available by 2027 at the latest.
welcome.login_text: If you do not have an account yet, you can create an account at the top right ("Login" → "Register") or request one by writing an email to {'xyz@123.de'} with a short explanation of your intended usecase.
welcome.format_text: Please note that SportVid currently only supports the analysis of mp4 video files to avoid long processing times due to transcoding videos on our server.

guidelines.title: Guidelines
guidelines.tutorial_hint_loggedin: Interactive step-by-step tutorials are available for all major workflows.
guidelines.tutorial_hint_loggedout: Interactive step-by-step tutorials are available for all major workflows. Log in and click the icon in the top right to get started.
guidelines.text:
1. How to Start
    1. Register or log in to your SportVid account.
    2. Upload a match or training video (mp4 format).
  2. How to Get Position Data
    1. Run the ByteTrack Plugin to automatically detect players and the ball in the video and generate bounding box tracks.
    2. Use the DLT + RANSAC Plugin to compute a homography matrix for top-view projection by annotating landmarks on the pitch.
    3. After calibration, positional data can be displayed on the top-view pitch.
    4. Alternatively, you can manually upload position data if it is already available in a supported format.
  3. Metric Computation
    1. Run the Metric Computation Plugin on existing position data to calculate metrics such as distance covered, speed, and acceleration per player.
    2. Select the position data source and optionally configure a smoothing filter for the position data before running.
  4. Visualizations
    1. Top View: Displays player positions on a 2D pitch view synchronized with the video. Use display settings to toggle player labels, trails, and team colors.
    2. Heatmap: Shows spatial activity density per player or team over a selectable time range.
    3. Metric Charts: Compare player metrics as a table or chart. Filter by player, team, or time interval.
  5. How to Export
    1. Use the export button in the app bar to download CSV files of raw or aggregated positional data (e.g., full match, 1st half, 2nd half).
    2. In the top-view, heatmap, and metric views you can save image snapshots or video exports.

experience_mode.heading: How do you want to use plugins?
experience_mode.simple_sentence: I just want to get started without worrying about technical details. Show me only what's essential.
experience_mode.complex_sentence: I know my way around machine learning / computer vision and want full control over every parameter.

upload_video.video_view: This is where all your uploaded videos are listed. Once uploaded, click on a video to open it in the analysis view.
upload_video.open_modal: Click here to open the video upload modal.
upload_video.fill_form: In the video upload modal, you can select a video file from your computer and fill in the required information about the video. Make sure to provide accurate information about the sport, division, age group, and field dimensions to ensure the best analysis results.
upload_video.upload_video: All required fields are filled — click the button to start the upload.
upload_video.video_processing: Your video is currently being processed. This may take some time depending on the video length and server load. Once processing is complete, it will be ready for analysis.

analyse_video.video_view: This is where all your uploaded videos are listed. Click the Analyse button on a video to open it in the analysis view.
analyse_video.video_player: This is the video player. You can play, pause and scrub through your video here. All visualizations can be synchronized to the current playback position.
analyse_video.top_view: This is the top-view panel. It shows position data projected onto a 2D field — players, paths and team assignments. Use the controls to select which data to display.
analyse_video.visualization_tabs: These tabs give you different ways to explore your data: Timeline for annotated events, Events for a structured event list, Heatmap for spatial density, and Metrics for player and team performance data.
analyse_video.appbar_actions: The toolbar gives you quick access to the main tools: run plugins to process your video, check the run history, manage annotation shortcuts, and export your data.

run_plugin.position_data: Actions that process your video now live right where their result is used, instead of behind a central menu. Here in the empty pitch view, you can generate position data — run ByteTrack for player tracking, set up a DLT+RANSAC camera calibration, or upload position data manually.
run_plugin.kpi_tab: Once position data is available, open the Metrics tab: computing metrics (distance covered, velocity, metabolic power, and more) happens inline, right there.

check_status.open_modal: Click here to open the plugin run history. This is where you can see the status of all your plugin runs — whether they are queued, running, completed, or if any errors occurred.
check_status.status_table: This table lists all plugin runs for the current video. Each row shows the plugin name, the date it was run, its progress, and its current status. You can use this to track ongoing runs or review past results.
check_status.delete_panel: Expand this section to delete plugin runs. You can delete all runs for your account, all runs for the current video, all runs of a specific plugin type for the current video, or select individual runs to remove. This is useful to clean up old or failed runs.

export.open_modal: Click here to open the export panel. Important: export options that rely on computed data — such as metrics or position data — will only work if that data has already been generated.
export.export_panel: The left panel lists all available export formats. You can export raw position data, computed metrics (regular or aggregated), merged or individual CSV files, or annotation formats like ELAN. Choose the format that fits your needs.
export.export_select: To select an export format, just click it in the list. For this tutorial, select 'Metrics (aggregated)'.
export.export_details: After selecting a format, you see its configuration options. Depending on the format, you may need to choose teams, time ranges, specific metrics, or other parameters. Once configured, click the Export button to download the file. Remember: if the required data hasn't been computed yet, the dropdowns will be empty and the export won't be possible.

dlt_ransac.intro:
Click here to open the DLT+RANSAC card. It computes a static camera calibration by mapping annotated landmark points from the pitch view to their corresponding positions in the video. This calibration is needed to convert pixel coordinates into real-world pitch coordinates, enabling accurate position data generation.

To apply it, you first need a calibration asset — a set of reference points defined on the pitch view.
dlt_ransac.create_select: If you don't have a calibration asset yet, click Create to set one up. Use Select to load an existing asset.
dlt_ransac.create_modal: Choose the calibration type: Marker uses individual landmark points (e.g. corner flags, penalty spots), Segment uses line segments. Select the type matching your setup, then click Create.
dlt_ransac.calibration_asset_btn: Via this button you can create a new calibration asset, save the current one, update an existing one, or switch to a different saved asset.
dlt_ransac.object_btn: This button shows your current calibration type (Marker or Segments). Click it to toggle the video marker overlay — this highlights reference landmarks on the pitch view. In Marker mode, you can also add custom markers or remove existing ones.
dlt_ransac.object_info:
Left-click a marker in the pitch view to open a zoomed video overlay, where you can precisely place it on the corresponding video position. Right-click a marker to de-toggle it and remove the video mapping.

Once all markers are set, save the asset via the Calibration Asset button, then go back to the empty pitch view and click Apply Calibration on the DLT+RANSAC card with the saved asset selected.

posdata_bytetrack.intro:
Click here to open the ByteTrack card. It performs object tracking directly on the video, detecting and tracking players and the ball frame by frame, generating bounding boxes for each detected object.

The tracking results can later be used together with a camera calibration (DLT+RANSAC) to compute real-world position data, which in turn enables metric computation.
posdata_bytetrack.fps:
Set the frames per second (FPS) used for tracking. The value is pre-set to your video's frame rate, which is the recommended choice. It ensures every frame is analyzed and no motion is missed.

You can freely adjust it: a lower FPS speeds up processing but may cause the tracker to lose fast-moving objects between frames. A higher FPS than the video's native rate has no benefit, as no additional information is available.
posdata_bytetrack.run_plugin: Click 'Start Tracking' to start the ByteTrack tracking. The progress can be tracked in the History panel or right here on the card. Once completed, the tracking results can be used for position data generation via Metric Computation.

posdata_manual.upload_open: Click the upload button to open the position data upload dialog.
posdata_manual.upload_modal: Fill in the required fields: give the data a name, select its format, and attach the corresponding file. Depending on the format, additional fields such as delimiter or coordinate origin may appear.
posdata_manual.format_select: Select the format that matches your position data file. Different providers use different conventions — choosing the correct format ensures the data is parsed and converted correctly.
posdata_manual.upload: Once all fields are filled in, click 'Upload'. The system will automatically run the Posdata Convert plugin afterwards to normalize the data into the internal format, making it available for visualization and metric computation.

kpi_computation.intro: Click here to open the metric computation card. It calculates performance metrics such as distance covered, velocity, metabolic power, equivalent distance, and centroid distance based on player position data.
kpi_computation.format_select: Select the data format that matches your position data source. Choosing 'SportVid' enables the ByteTrack run and calibration selectors below. All other formats use an externally uploaded position data file.
kpi_computation.tracking_data:
Select the position data to use for the computation. This dropdown lists the position data files that have been uploaded or generated for this video.

If you selected 'SportVid' as the format, you will instead see a ByteTrack run and calibration asset selector. Choose the corresponding run and the calibration asset used during tracking.
kpi_computation.advanced_options: The 'Advanced Options' panel lets you configure an optional smoothing filter for the position data before computing metrics. You can choose between a 'Butterworth lowpass' or a 'Savitzky-Golay lowpass' filter, and adjust their hyperparameters. If you are unsure, leaving this at 'None' is a good default.
kpi_computation.run_plugin: Click 'Compute Metrics' to start the metric computation. The progress can be tracked in the History panel. Once completed, results will appear right here in the Metrics tab.

top_view.pitch_overview: The top-view shows your position data projected onto a 2D area — this could be a soccer pitch, a handball court, a basketball court, a climbing wall, or any other defined playing field. Each tracked entity appears as a colored dot, grouped and colored by team or assignment.
top_view.controls: When the top-view is not synchronized with the video player, you can control playback independently. Use the play button to start or pause, and the slider below to seek to any position. The time code next to the download button shows the current position within the position dataset.
top_view.display_settings_open: Click Display Settings to open the customization menu.
top_view.display_settings:
The Display Settings menu lets you adjust everything about how the top-view looks:

Playback: Toggle synchronization with the video player, or set a time offset to align position data and video.

Visibility: Show or hide bounding boxes (if available), player IDs on the dots, or toggle individual players and teams on/off. You can also adjust team colors.

Metric Overlays (View Metrics submenu): Overlay computed metrics like Space Control (Voronoi-based) or Effective Playing Space (convex hull) directly on the field.

Area & Grid: Switch between different predefined area sizes, or configure longitudinal and transverse grid lines.

Position Data: Upload a new position data file or switch to a different already-loaded dataset.
top_view.download: Click the download button to save a screenshot of the current top-view frame as an image file.

heatmap.tab_switch: The Heatmap tab visualizes the spatial distribution of player positions over time.
heatmap.pitch_overview: This is the playing field. The heatmap or movement trace is rendered directly on top of it. The displayed area can be adjusted — for example, you can zoom in to show only one half of the pitch.
heatmap.player_legend: Below the pitch you can select which players to include in the visualization. Click an individual player dot to toggle them on or off. Click a team name to select or deselect the entire team at once.
heatmap.settings:
The toolbar above the pitch gives you several controls:

Area size: switch between the full field and sub-areas such as one half or one penalty box.
Display mode: toggle between a classic heatmap (density overlay) and a movement trace (individual dot paths).
Save: export a high-resolution screenshot of the current visualization.
Time sync: quickly sync the start or end of the time window to the current video position, or jump to the full match, first half, or second half.
heatmap.time_selector:
The time range selector (right) and the sync menu (left) work together to filter the heatmap to any time window.

Drag the left or right handle on the range selector to set the start and end time. The sync menu lets you snap either handle to the current video position for frame-accurate selection, or jump instantly to the full match, first half, or second half.

kpi_visualization.tab_switch: The Metrics tab gives you two complementary views of your computed metrics. Let's explore both.
kpi_visualization.table_view: The table view shows aggregated statistics per player or per team. Each team gets its own card with a data table. Use the player dots at the top of each card to filter which players are included. Toggle between per-player and per-team grouping using the toolbar.
kpi_visualization.chart_view: The chart view shows metric values as a time series across the match. You can plot multiple metrics simultaneously (e.g. running distance per frame alongside metabolic power). Use the player selection legend at the bottom to show or hide individual players or entire teams.
kpi_visualization.settings:
The toolbar gives you full control over what is displayed:

Table / Chart toggle: switch between the table summary and the time-series chart.
Player / Team grouping: group results by individual player or aggregate by team.
Metric selection: choose which metrics to show. In chart mode you can also pick windowed variants (rolling window over N frames).
Zone selection: restrict the analysis to specific pitch zones.
Download: export the current chart as an image (chart mode only).
Time sync: snap the time window to the video position or jump to a predefined half.
kpi_visualization.time_selector:
The time range selector (right) and the sync menu (left) work together to filter all metric data to any time window.

Drag the left or right handle to set the start and end time. Use the sync menu to snap either handle to the current video position for frame-accurate selection, or jump instantly to the full match, first half, or second half.

position_data_generation.video_select: Select a video from the list to open the analysis view.
position_data_generation.choose_path: How do you want to provide position data?
position_data_generation.manual_upload: Use the upload button to import your position data file. See the Position Data (Manual) tutorial for a detailed walkthrough.
position_data_generation.select_dlt: This is the DLT+RANSAC calibration button. If you don't have a calibration asset yet, create one first — the DLT+RANSAC tutorial walks you through this step by step.
position_data_generation.select_bytetrack: Now click this ByteTrack button to open its card, set the FPS to match your video's frame rate, then click Start Tracking to generate position data. See the ByteTrack tutorial for a detailed walkthrough.

plugin.title: Plugins
plugin.shot_timeline_hint: Annotations are created based on shot boundaries of the selected timeline.
plugin.scalar_timeline_hint: The scalar values of the selected timelines will be aggregated.
plugin.position_data_attribute_hint: Timestamp (ms), Player-ID, and X/Y coordinates are always included. Optionally add more attributes.
plugin.kpi_names_hint: Select which metrics to include (min. 1 required).
plugin.kpi_attribute_hint: Timestamp (ms) and Player-ID are always included. Optionally add more attributes.
plugin.kpi_aggregated_attribute_hint: Player-ID is always included. Optionally add more attributes.

aggregation.plugin_description:
This plugin allows you to combine information from multiple timeles with logical operators. In this way, more complex patterns can be revealed. For example, the logical and can be used to detect when two concepts or persons are visible simultaneously.

Tip: You can perform the plugin multiple times to create more complex patterns. The following example performs three aggregations to detect when a Concept A is simultaneously visible with Concept B or Concept C:

AGG1 = (Concept A) Logical And (Concept B)
AGG2 = (Concept A) Logical And (Concept C)
AGG3 = (AGG1) Logical Or (AGG2)

bytetrack.plugin_description: This plugin performs multi-object tracking (MOT). It uses the 'bytetrack_x_mot17' model from https://github.com/ifzhang/ByteTrack.

object_tracker.plugin_description:
This plugin performs multi-object tracking (MOT) directly on the video. It detects and tracks players and the ball frame by frame, generating bounding boxes for each detected object. The detector model used for the underlying object detection, as well as its parameters and the tracker parameters, can be freely configured.

The tracking results can later be used together with a camera calibration (DLT+RANSAC) to compute real-world position data.

team_clustering.plugin_description: This plugin assigns the player tracks from a previous player-tracking run to teams via color clustering (K-Means or HDBSCAN) based on jersey colors. It doesn't run its own tracker but reuses the bounding boxes of a completed Object Tracking run.
team_clustering.object_tracker_id_hint: Select a completed player-tracking (Object Tracking) run for this video.
team_clustering.object_tracker_run_none: No completed Object Tracking run found.

osnet_reid.plugin_description: This plugin re-identifies player tracks from a previous player-tracking run across track-ID switches (e.g. after occlusions or players leaving/re-entering the field), using an appearance-based feature extractor (OSNet) and an online gallery of identity prototypes. It doesn't run its own tracker but reuses the bounding boxes of a completed Object Tracking run.
osnet_reid.object_tracker_id_hint: Select a completed player-tracking (Object Tracking) run for this video.

calibration_static_dlt.plugin_description: This plugin performs a static calibration of the video using the Direct Linear Transformation (DLT) + RANSAC method. It uses the annotated marker correspondences from a calibration asset to estimate the homography matrix.
calibration_static_dlt.calibration_id_hint: Select a calibration asset to use for the calibration.

kpi_computation.plugin_description:
This plugin computes selected performance metrics based on the position data. The computation is performed using the floodlight package. The following metrics are currently available:

Distance Covered, Velocity, Metabolic Power, Equivalent Distance, & Distance to the Team Centroid.
kpi_computation.tracking_data_id_hint: Select a position dataset to use for the computation.
kpi_computation.object_tracker_run_id_hint: Select a completed Object Tracker run to use for the computation.
kpi_computation.object_tracker_run_none: No completed Object Tracker runs found.
kpi_computation.calibration_id_hint: Select the calibration asset used to map video positions to top-view coordinates.

audio_waveform.plugin_description: This plugin computes the waveform of the audio signal for basic sound analysis.

audio_rms.plugin_description: This plugin computes the audio volume by computing the root mean square (RMS) of the audio signal. It could, for example, reveal scenes with silence or sudden volume changes in a film.

whisper.plugin_description: This plugin uses OpenAI's Whisper model to automatically provide a transcription of the spoken language in the video. It supports more than 100 languages. A list of supported languages can be found here.
whisper.temperature_fallback: Retry degenerate output at higher temperature
whisper.no_repeat_ngram_size: Forbid repeating word sequences of length

audio_frequency.plugin_description: This plugin computes the spectrogram of the audio signal that could reveal rhytmic patterns (e.g., music), voices, or other sound patterns.
audio_frequency.n_fft: Length of the FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) window

blip.plugin_description:
This plugin uses the large vision language model InstructBLIP that is similar to GPT-4 to perform question answering over the video. It can be used for various purposes, for example, to automatically find concepts within the video. Here are some examples:

Does this image show a car? Please answer with yes or no!
Does this image show at least three persons? Please answer with yes or no!
Is this photo taken in a restaurant? Please answer with yes or no!

clip.plugin_description:
This plugin uses OpenAI's CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining) model that allows to search the video content for arbritrary visual concepts given a textual description. The textual description should describe the concept of interest in simple, unambigous terms. Here is an example: A photo of a car.

CLIP works well for a large variety of concepts (e.g., objects, places, events, daytimes, weather conditions, etc.) that can be identified from a single video frame. To identify concepts that require temporal context from the video such as human actions, we recommend using the "Action Recognition" plugin.

Please note that the plugin required more time if you first use it for a video. After the first use, the results will be computed much faster.

clip_ontology.plugin_description:
This plugin uses OpenAI's CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining) model that allows to search the video content for a set of arbritrary visual concepts given a csv file containing the concept name and an associated textual description. The textual description should describe the concept of interest in simple, unambigous terms. Here is an example:

"day","a photo taken at daylight"
"night","a photo taken during the night"

It works well for a large variety of concepts (e.g., objects, places, events, daytimes, weather conditions, etc.) that can be identified from a single video frame. To identify concepts that require temporal context from the video such as human actions, we recommend using the "Action Recognition" plugin.

Please note that the plugin required more time if you first use it for a video. After the first use, the results will be computed much faster.
clip_ontology.concepts_hint: Csv file with timeline name and a description for the concept in each row

x_clip.plugin_description:
This plugin uses X-CLIP that allows to search the video content for arbritrary actions given a textual description. The textual description should describe the action in simple, unambigous terms. Here is an example: A video showing a person dancing

Please note that the plugin required more time if you first use it for a video. After the first use, the results will be computed much faster.

color_analysis.plugin_description: This plugin uses a clustering algorithm (k-Means) to determine the top-k dominant colors within the video. The number of dominant colors can be selected by the slider below.
color_analysis.max_iter: Maximum Number of Iterations for k-Means Clustering

color_brightness_analysis.plugin_description: This plugin computes the brightness of frames within the video. It can reveal darker and brighter content that can, for example, reveal the daytime of a scene.

face_clustering.plugin_description:
This plugin automatically performs a clustering algorithm to automatically determine the dominant faces (persons) in the video. Selecting the threshold for clustering is crucial to achieve good results. After performing the clustering, each resulting cluster visible in the tab "Faces" should ideally only contain images of the same person. If this is not the case, the threshold needs to be lowered so that fewer images are grouped in the same cluster.

Note that after performing the clustering, the clusters can be manually adjusted and a person constellation graph can be created in the tab "Faces". Moreover, you can create a timeline for a specific person to see when the person is visible in the video.

faceemotion.plugin_description:
This plugin automaticalyl recognizes the facial expression for each face found in the video. It differentiates between seven basic emotions: Angry, Disgust, Fear, Happy, Sad, Surprise, and Neutral.

Please note that there can be multiple faces visible at the same time. The timelines created by this plugin show that maximum score for each emotion over all faces visible at the same time.

face_identification.plugin_name: Face Identification with an Example Image
face_identification.plugin_description:
This plugin perform a face identification based on an uploaded example image of the person of interest. Please note that the image must be uploaded as a jpg file and that it should only contain the person you are interested in. The plugin might fail, if the face is not detected in your uploaded photo. So, please make sure that the face is clearly and entirely visible.

To automatically identify the main characters within the video, we recommend using the "Face Clustering" plugin.
face_identification.query_images_hint: *The image should only the person you want to search for in good resolution and quality

place_clustering.plugin_description:
This plugin automatically performs a clustering algorithm to automatically determine the dominant places in the video. Selecting the threshold for clustering is crucial to achieve good results. After performing the clustering, each resulting cluster visible in the tab "Places" should ideally only contain images of the same place. If this is not the case, the threshold needs to be lowered so that fewer images are grouped in the same cluster.

Note that after performing the clustering, the clusters can be manually adjusted and a constellation graph can be created. Moreover, you can create a timeline for a specific place to see when the place is visible in the video.

places_classification.plugin_description: This plugin uses a model trained on the Places365 dataset to identify places within the video in three hierarchy levels with 3, 16, and 365 place categories. The first hierarchy level contains the places: indoor, outdoor natural, and outdoor man-made. The set of place categories in the other levels can be found here.

shot_detection.plugin_description: This plugin automatically detects shots boundaries within the video using a deep learning model. You can create or merge cuts by right-clicking on the resulting timeline.

shot_density.plugin_description: This plugin predicts the density of the shots within a video. In this way, you can differentiate between slow and fast-paced scenes. The computation is performed based on a selected timeline, e.g., the timeline that is created by the "Shot Boundary Detection" plugin.

shot_scalar_annotation.plugin_description: This plugin annotates shots based on a selected shot timeline with the average value of a timeline with scalar values. This plugin can be primarily used to import information created within TIB-AV-A to ELAN.

shot_type_classification.plugin_description:
This plugin predicts the shot sizes within the video based on a deep learning model. It differentiates between five shots sizes: Extreme Close-Up, Close-Up, Medium Shot, Full Shot, and Long Shot.

By selecting a timeline that contains shots, e.g., the timeline that is created by the "Shot Boundary Detection" plugin, each shot will be automatically labeled by its dominant shot size.

thumbnail.plugin_description: This plugin creates thumbnails for the video that are used in the tab "Shots". The plugin is automatically performed once a video is uploaded. Please only perform it again if the thumbnails appear to be missing.

invert.plugin_description: Inverts a timeline by calculating 1-y. If the original timeline was greater than 1 or less than 0, the values are normalized to [0,1] beforehand.
